keyVerseText: And next him were Eden, and Miniamin, and Jeshua, and Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in their set office, to give to their brethren by courses, as well to the great as to the small: next: Heb. at his hand set: or, trust
rootMeaning: The Hebrew word מִנְיָמִין (Minyâmîyn) is derived from the preposition מִן (min), meaning 'from' or 'out of,' combined with יָמִין (yamin), meaning 'right hand.' Literally, it signifies 'from the right hand,' a phrase that in ancient Near Eastern culture often connotes a position of honor, strength, or authority. This etymology enriches the understanding of the term beyond a mere name, suggesting a symbolic association with favor or trusted standing.
usageInScripture: The word מִנְיָמִין appears three times in Scripture, always as a proper noun referring to individuals named Miniamin. These references include a Levite during King Hezekiah's reign and a priest present at Nehemiah's dedication of Jerusalem's wall. The consistent translations—'and Miniamin,' 'of Miniamin,' and simply 'Miniamin'—indicate its use as a personal name rather than a common noun, underscoring its identity function within priestly and Levitical contexts.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding מִנְיָמִין as 'from the right hand' invites reflection on the biblical symbolism of the right hand as a place of power, protection, and divine blessing. The individuals bearing this name served in sacred roles during pivotal moments in Israel's history, highlighting God's provision of faithful servants positioned at His right hand to uphold worship and community order. For the Christian faith, this reminds believers of Christ's exaltation at the right hand of God and calls them to serve faithfully in their God-ordained roles, trusting in His strength and authority.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Chronicles 31:15, Miniamin is listed among priests responsible for distributing provisions to their brethren, described as being 'at his hand set' or 'in trust.' The name Miniamin here emphasizes the entrusted responsibility these priests held, symbolically standing at the right hand—an honored and reliable position. This highlights the importance of faithful stewardship and trustworthiness in service to God's people, reflecting the deeper meaning embedded in the name itself.
